I make soup, and the house feels very warm now.

The sky becomes wider, bluer, and much more forgiving now.

I plant a seed, and hope follows quietly after me.

The grass is dry, and the hot air shimmers softly.
I eat watermelon, and sweet juice runs down my chin.

The lake holds the afternoon in a cool deep blue.
I swim until the sun touches the far distant hills.
A fan turns slowly, moving warm air in a circle.
The night smells strongly of cut grass and warm skin.

Summer ends with a sudden and very cool evening wind.
Autumn arrives with red leaves and very crisp cool air.
The apples fall before I can catch them all quickly.
A squirrel buries an acorn, looking serious and very quickly.
I rake the leaves, and the yard changes its shape.
The light turns amber, soft on all the waiting faces.
Geese fly far south in a long and gray line.

I put on a sweater, and the day feels kinder.

If you read it, you have entered a little space.
The last line is also a quiet and small beginning.
I leave the words here, like stones in a stream.
Thank you for walking this long far way with me.
Now I stop, and the deep silence returns softly now.
